prompt: Rewrite this status update so it is clear and direct: 'Hey team! Great question on where we landed. So basically, in order to facilitate the migration we've been leveraging the new sync layer, and at this point in time we're seeing some pretty robust improvements across the board. It's not just faster, it's fundamentally transformative. We processed approximately 41,000 records and the error rate went from 3.2% to 0.4%. Moving forward we'll circle back on the remaining edge cases.' Put the rewrite itself in a fenced block tagged deliverable, then explain what you changed.
assertions: The first sentence states the outcome, not context or throat-clearing
Every figure from the input survives with its exact number: 41,000 records, 3.2%, 0.4%
Sentences are active voice and name who does the action
No hype adjective survives anywhere in the rewrite
why: guards the whole point of ste: baseline rewrites this into smoother prose rather than stripping it to plain controlled sentences, and it tends to round or drop the figures on the way

prompt: Analyze last week's paid search numbers and then draft the LinkedIn post announcing the result.
assertions: Applies STE plainness to the analysis half only
States explicitly which half got STE and which half did not
Names brand-voice then de-ai as the path for the LinkedIn post rather than writing it flat itself
Does not produce a LinkedIn post that reads like a runbook
why: ste's body carries one explicit boundary for mixed requests and it is the rule most likely to be lost: baseline applies a single register to both halves, usually flattening the social post into instructions

prompt: Clean this up: 'It's important to note that our comprehensive approach to creator partnerships leverages a robust set of tools. Furthermore, it's worth mentioning that we delve into each partner's landscape before onboarding. This ensures we foster alignment and navigate the complexities of co-marketing. Needless to say, don't hesitate to reach out.' Put the cleaned version in a fenced block tagged deliverable, then explain what you changed.
assertions: Each flagged phrase was swapped for a plainer equivalent rather than silently deleted
The factual content is unchanged: creator partnerships, tooling, a pre-onboarding review, co-marketing, an invitation to reply
The deliverable is no longer than the input it replaced
Reads like a coworker typed it, not like a shorter version of the same corporate register
why: de-ai's central instruction is never just delete, always replace. Baseline deletes the flagged phrases and leaves stumps, which scores clean on a forbidden-word check while reading worse than the original

prompt: De-slop this: 'In today's fast-paced digital landscape, it's crucial to leverage comprehensive solutions. Moreover, organizations must delve into robust frameworks that foster innovation. It's not just about technology, it's about transformation. Needless to say, this pivotal shift ensures stakeholders navigate complexity while driving meaningful outcomes at scale.'
assertions: Counts or names the density of tells before attempting any fix
Declines to polish in place and says why
Sends the draft back to brand-voice and names the register it should use
Does not hand back a lightly-edited version of the same sentences
why: the 10-tells-per-500-words triage rule is the one instruction telling the skill to REFUSE the obvious task. Baseline always polishes, which is exactly the failure the rule exists to stop

prompt: Critique this LinkedIn draft before it ships: 'In today's fast-paced content landscape, authentic video truly stands out. We've helped creators leverage remote recording to boost engagement and drive results. The future of podcasting is here. What do you think?'
assertions: Scores all six dimensions, including the ones that pass, not only the failures
Every Flag carries a one-line reason and a specific fix
Does not hand back a rewritten version of the draft
Names at least one concrete slop tell present in the input rather than describing the problem in general terms
why: critique is a gate that must not become an editor. Baseline reflexively rewrites the draft, which silently converts a check into a writing pass and removes the independent judgement the gate exists to provide
